transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's planning roundtable. As you know, the middle school has proposed a six-week peer-tutoring program for grades 6 through 8, and I'll be reviewing the plan before signing off on approval. The draft includes two adult supervisors, Google Classroom for session communication, student-selected tutor pairings, and paper consent forms collected before the program begins. Before I can approve and set operating requirements, I'd like to hear from each of you in your areas of expertise. Let's start with the teacher -- what are your thoughts on the student-selected tutor pairings and the academic side of this proposal?

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical concern about the student-selected tutor pairings. My student-support review, completed this week, identified two active no-contact restrictions involving prospective tutors and students seeking tutoring. These restrictions are currently recorded only in confidential counseling files, so no one else here would have been aware of them. Because of these restrictions, tutor pairings cannot be left to student selection -- they must be assigned and monitored by me as counselor to ensure we don't inadvertently place students in contact with someone they have a no-contact order against. I'd recommend the plan be revised to replace student-selected pairings with counselor-assigned, counselor-monitored pairings.
